name: Mocha and banded ware
region: Staffordshire, Yorkshire and Tyneside, England; later Britain and North America
summary: Cheap pale earthenware for the tavern and the farm kitchen. Bands of coloured slip are turned on a lathe, and a drop of acid colour spreads into a fern or a tree.

philosophy.core_thesis: A machine can turn the bands of a dipped jug in one pass, and one drop of acid colour on a wet slip makes a tree that no hand can plan.
design_principles: Throw or press the body in creamware or pearlware, with a wall 4 to 6 mm thick.
Dip the leather-hard pot in a slip of one colour, then turn bands in slip on a lathe.
Cut the bands 3 to 15 mm wide, in groups of 2 or 3, in contrast of fawn, blue, green or brown.
Make the mocha tree: touch the wet slip with a drop of tobacco, turpentine and iron-oxide colour; it feathers upward in 2 seconds.
Put the tree between two bands, once or three times round a mug.
Dip the whole piece in a clear lead glaze and fire it at about 1100 °C.
Keep the shapes plain: a mug or a jug should hold a half, one or two pints.
anti_patterns: A white ground with no slip band
A hand-painted flower in the band
A cold colour with no earth tone

form.shape: Cylindrical mugs and tankards, straight-sided jugs, bowls, measures and large mixing bowls made as pints and quarts.
form.profile: A straight or slightly flared wall on a flat base; a jug has a short neck and a strap handle with a foot.
form.foot_and_rim: A plain flat base with a small turned foot ring; the rim is a plain bead with a spout for the jug.
form.proportion: A pint mug stands 11 to 13 cm high; the wall is 4 to 6 mm thick, which is thin for earthenware.
rules: Keep the wall straight, so that the lathe can cut the bands in a clean line.
Place the tree in a band of one colour between two bands of another.
Glaze the inside and the outside.

bodies.rule: Use a pale earthenware that fires cream or pearl white, so that the slip colours show. Keep dark red and stoneware bodies out: they hide the bands.

methods: throwing and jolleying on the wheel
turning bands on an engine lathe
pouring a mocha colour on the wet slip
forming.joins: Handles are moulded or pulled and fixed with slip; the rim is turned smooth with a metal rib.
forming.details: A turned band as sharp as a line, a tree that feathers up to a band, and a small foot ring cut by the lathe.

glaze.pattern: Fine turned bands in two or three colours, wide bands with a mocha tree, and a seaweed or cat's-eye pattern; some pots show marbling.
glaze.gloss: A clear gloss of about 55 to 80 GU, with a slight yellow cast.
glaze.wear: The slip bands wear at the rim and the foot; the tree stays fresh because the glaze covers it.

palette.strategy: Earth tones in bands on a pale ground: fawn, brown, ochre, blue and green, with a dark tree in one band.

firing.kiln: A coal-fired bottle kiln; biscuit, slip decoration and a second firing for the glaze.
processes: turning the bands on a lathe
adding the mocha tree on wet slip
firing.scale: Pubs in England and America used pottery measures in the thousands; the ware was made by the million between 1790 and 1880.
firing.signs: Sharp lathe bands, a mocha tree that feathers, and a base that has a turned ring.

pieces.form: Straight-sided jug with fawn and blue bands and a mocha tree
Large bowl with three turned bands in brown, ochre and cream
Cylindrical jar with a banded wall and a marbled shoulder
Water jug with a wide fawn band and a tree in black

positive: fern-like mocha tree in a band
turned bands in fawn, blue and brown
still-life museum photograph, soft north light

canonical_works.work: Mocha mug with a tree in a fawn band
Banded jug with a mocha tree

emotion.target_response: A plain, cheerful ease: the viewer sees crisp bands and a small tree and thinks of a tavern table and a morning jug.

use_cases: a tavern or kitchen set dressing of 1800
a museum label on mocha ware
a mug or jug brief that needs earth-tone bands
avoid_when: the brief needs hand-trailed slip pictures
the brief needs a printed pattern

modifiers.request: blue and white bands, twentieth century
modifiers.how: Change to a white earthenware with four blue bands in one pattern; drop the mocha tree.
Replace the bands with blue or green sponge-stamped colour on a white body.

wall_thickness.note: A lathe can cut thin wall that earthenware slip does not allow by hand.
